findings.evidence: Mathlib proves `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite` at `Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Span.lean:128`, and its analogous `Module.FinitePresentation.of_localizationSpan'` removes finiteness from the public theorem using exactly this reduction at `Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Finiteness.lean:229-238`; finiteness is used here only to obtain a uniform exponent at lines 175-176.
findings.fix: Remove `[Finite s]`: extract a finite subcover using `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, apply a finite-cover helper, then use overlap compatibility and local uniqueness to prove the resulting point agrees with `N r` for every remaining `r : s`.
findings.issue: `exists_map_eq_of_isLocalized_span` assumes `[Finite s]`, making the advertised sheaf gluing result weaker than its natural form for arbitrary unit-spanning standard covers.

summary: The gluing theorem unnecessarily restricts the covering set to be finite, although a unit-spanning set automatically contains a finite unit-spanning subcover.
